titre_page: How to make a two-player game on one tablet? | Yop2D guide
description: Make a two-player game on one tablet in Yop2D, without code: two joysticks, each one moving its own character, thanks to multi-touch.
h1: How to make a two-player game on one tablet?
carte: Each player uses their own thumb: two joysticks on the same screen, each one moving its own character.
etapes: One on each side of the screen.
“Object to move” field in the Inspector.
blocs: On a tablet, two people can play at the same time: **each player has their own joystick** and their own character. Yop2D follows each finger separately (multi-touch), so both characters move together, **without any node**.
a project open in the editor (landscape, ideally on a tablet);
two characters, for example **player1** and **player2** (two {{lang:obj_prefix_image}} objects);
a floor or a background, as you like.
Step 1: two characters that walk by themselves
Select **player1**, then tap **⚙ Object behavior** in the Inspector.
Add a **{{lang:obj_prefix_joystick}}** object to the scene (category **{{lang:cat_interactifs}}**) and put it at the bottom left.
Add a second one and put it at the bottom right.
Give them clear names: **joystick1** and **joystick2** (the last step explains why this helps).
A different color for each joystick helps the players: in the Inspector, change the color of each one.
Step 3: one target for each joystick
Select **joystick1**. In the Inspector, section **[[lang:insp_sep_joystick]]**, tap the **[[lang:insp_label_cible_joystick]]** button and choose **player1**.
Select **joystick2** and choose **player2** the same way.
Put one finger on each joystick: **both characters move at the same time**, each one with its own joystick. Lift one finger and only that character stops.
A finger that holds a joystick keeps it until you lift it, even if it slides outside the circle. It cannot take the other joystick.
Go further: read each joystick in a formula

The first joystick keeps its usual formulas: `joystick.x`, `joystick.y`, `joystick.force`, `joystick.angle`, `joystick.actif`. For the others, **give the joystick a name that starts with “joy”**, then use the same words after the name: `joystick2.x`, `joystick2.y`, `joystick2.force`, `joystick2.angle`, `joystick2.actif`.
For example, to move an object that is not a character with the second joystick, use [[pousser]] linked to [[NoeudEventChaqueImage]] with `=joystick2.x * 5` and `=joystick2.y * 5`.
Two ninjas on a meadow with two joysticks at the bottom, one blue and one orange
The “Two players” template: one joystick for each player.
A joystick named like this no longer gives its screen position with `.x` and `.y`: they give the direction pushed (between -1 and 1).

Platform characters can also have **their own jump button**: in ⚙ Object behavior, choose a different button for each character in **Jump button**. Multi-touch lets both players press at the same time.
The “Two players” template shows all this ready to use: two ninjas, two joysticks, and no node.
**Both characters follow the same joystick:** check that each joystick has its **own** target in **[[lang:insp_label_cible_joystick]]**.
**A character does not move:** its behavior must be **Top-down character** or **Platform character**, with **Controls: Joystick**.
**A joystick does not react:** make sure it is visible and not hidden behind another object.
**Only one joystick works:** check that you are using version 1266 or newer of Yop2D.
